    1→# Aethyme Core\n     2→\n     3→Last Updated: 2026-03-06\n     4→\n     5→Aethyme Core is the backend product in this repository.\n     6→\n     7→It owns:\n     8→\n     9→1. repository indexing\n    10→2. graph persistence and traversal\n    11→3. search, ego graph, and impact analysis\n    12→4. scorecard analysis\n    13→5. controlled autofix tooling from the CLI\n    14→6. deterministic navigation primitives for AI agents\n    15→\n    16→## Canonical Model\n    17→\n    18→`Platform > Org > Tenant > Repository > Graph`\n    19→\n    20→Runtime isolation is tenant-scoped.\n    21→\n    22→## Language Direction\n    23→\n    24→Aethyme is moving toward:\n    25→\n    26→- Rust for deterministic engine components\n    27→- Python for API, CLI, auth enforcement, scorecard orchestration, and SDKs\n    28→\n    29→See [`docs/architecture/rust-transition.md`](docs/architecture/rust-transition.md) and [`rust/README.md`](rust/README.md).\n    30→\n    31→## Auth Boundary\n    32→\n    33→- cloud owns login, registration, sessions, and user lifecycle\n    34→- core validates bearer credentials and API keys\n    35→- core enforces `org`, `tenant_id`, and `scopes`\n    36→- local development can mint a cloud-issued token for an existing user via `POST /api/auth/dev/token`\n    37→\n    38→## Active Surface\n    39→\n    40→### Core Logic\n    41→- `src/indexer`\n    42→- `src/indexing`\n    43→- `src/graph`\n    44→- `src/models`\n    45→- `src/scorecard`\n    46→- `src/autofixers`\n    47→- `rust`\n    48→\n    49→### Delivery\n    50→- `src/api`\n    51→- `src/cli.py`\n    52→- `sdk/python`\n    53→\n    54→### Verification\n    55→- `tests/api`\n    56→- `tests/queries`\n    57→- `tests/indexing`\n    58→- `tests/scorecard`\n    59→- `tests/autofixers`\n    60→\n    61→## Current Standard\n    62→\n    63→Only document and defend the verified path:\n    64→\n    65→- trusted bearer token or API key required\n    66→- `POST /api/v1/index/repositories`\n    67→- `POST /api/v1/search/`\n    68→- `POST /api/v1/ego/`\n    69→- `POST /api/v1/impact/`\n    70→- `POST /api/v1/scorecard/scan`\n    71→\n    72→API and CLI indexing both run through [`src/indexing/service.py`](src/indexing/service.py).\n    73→\n    74→## Local-First Workflow\n    75→\n    76→For the first product proof, Aethyme can run against one local repository without any SaaS layer.\n    77→\n    78→Core commands:\n    79→\n    80→- `aethyme repo ingest /path/to/repo`\n    81→- `aethyme repo inspect /path/to/repo --json-output`\n    82→- `aethyme repo clear-cache /path/to/repo`\n    83→- `aethyme query symbol /path/to/repo main`\n    84→- `aethyme query deps /path/to/repo src/main.py`\n    85→- `aethyme graph node /path/to/repo src/main.py --json-output`\n    86→- `aethyme graph children /path/to/repo GameEngine --json-output`\n    87→- `aethyme graph callers /path/to/repo fn:REPO:path:main --json-output`\n    88→- `aethyme graph docs /path/to/repo src/main.py --json-output`\n    89→- `aethyme task pack --repo /path/to/repo --task \"Explain this repo\" --json-output`\n    90→- `aethyme task explain --repo /path/to/repo`\n    91→- `aethyme task anchors --repo /path/to/repo --task \"Update validate_token flow\" --json-output`\n    92→- `aethyme task scope --repo /path/to/repo --task \"Update validate_token flow\" --json-output`\n    93→- `aethyme task next --repo /path/to/repo --task \"Update validate_token flow\" --json-output`\n    94→- `aethyme task expand --repo /path/to/repo --node src/auth.py --json-output`\n    95→- `aethyme eval explain-repo --repo /path/to/repo --json-output`\n    96→- `aethyme eval explain-repo --repo /path/to/repo --baseline-cmd \"<cmd>\" --aethyme-cmd \"<cmd>\"`\n    97→- `aethyme eval navigation-ctf --repo /path/to/repo --json-output`\n    98→\n    99→Codex runner example:\n   100→\n   101→- `aethyme eval explain-repo --repo /path/to/repo --baseline-cmd \"packages/aethyme/.venv/bin/python packages/aethyme/scripts/eval/run_codex_eval.py\" --aethyme-cmd \"packages/aethyme/.venv/bin/python packages/aethyme/scripts/eval/run_codex_eval.py\"`\n   102→\n   103→This local path is the shortest route to proving:\n   104→\n   105→1. repository mapping\n   106→2. discoverability\n   107→3. graph-mediated navigation\n   108→4. deterministic task-context packs\n   109→5. explain-repo evaluation artifacts\n   110→\n   111→Runtime notes:\n   112→\n   113→- the Python layer now executes a built Rust binary rather than `cargo run` for every call\n   114→- local repo artifacts are cached by snapshot key under `AETHYME_CACHE_DIR` or `/tmp/aethyme-cache`\n   115→- Git repositories use commit plus dirty-state metadata for cache keys instead of a full recursive fingerprint on every call\n   116→- `eval explain-repo` can execute real baseline and Aethyme runs when `--baseline-cmd` and `--aethyme-cmd` are provided\n   117→- external runners receive `AETHYME_EVAL_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_FILE`, `AETHYME_EVAL_TOOL_REPO`, and `AETHYME_EVAL_TOOL_PYTHON` so Codex-style wrappers can enforce structured output and call back into Aethyme\n   118→- the bundled Codex wrapper cleans its temporary prompt/event/schema files automatically; Chau7-driven runs should also close their MCP-controlled tab once the report artifact is captured and the tab is idle\n   119→- without those commands, it still emits the comparison artifacts only\n   120→- the Aethyme-assisted prompt now uses a compact rendered context-pack view instead of injecting the full raw pack\n   121→- every `eval explain-repo` run writes a markdown report under `packages/aethyme/docs/reports/evals/`\n   122→- the report includes the explanation, prompts, pack JSON, and verbose run results\n   123→- eval outputs now include a structured output schema, scoring rubric, and reference answer\n   124→\n   125→## Start except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:\n    65→            raise ValueError(\n    66→                \"Invalid scopes JSON in AETHYME_DB_SCOPES/REPOGRAPH_DB_SCOPES\"\n    67→            ) from exc\n resolved_scopes.append(scope_value)\n    79→        return resolved_scopes\n    80→\n    81→    def apply_session(self, cur: Any) -> None:\n    82→        \"\"\"Public wrapper for setting session Authentication & Authorization** (`src/auth/`)\n- **JWT Token Verification:** Aethyme-issued tokens with tenant claims\n- **OIDC Support:** Fallback to OIDC if configured\n- **API Keys:** `rg_` prefixed keys with scoped permissions\n- **User Context:** Contains `user_id`, `tenant_id`, `scopes`, `org_id`, `email`\n- **Scope System:** `repo:read`, `repo:write`, `org:admin` privileges\n- **Tenant Isolation:** All operations scoped by tenant; row-level security via PostgreSQL\n\n#### **2. Graph Storage & Queries** (`src/graph/`)\n- **Backend:** PostgreSQL with thread-safe connection pooling\n- **GraphStore Class:** Multi-tenant graph operations\n  - `create_repository()` - Register repos with languages\n  - `search()` - Full-text & fuzzy symbol search\n  - `ego_graph()` - Connected nodes up to depth N\n  - `impact_analysis()` - Affected symbols on changes\n  - Row-level security via session variables (`app.current_tenant`, `app.current_org`)\n\n#### **3. Repository Indexing** (`src/indexing/`)\n- **Service Layer:** `RepositoryIndexRequest` canonical contract (used by API + CLI)\n- **Rust Engine Integration:** Binary invocation via `indexing/engine.py`\n  - Automatic compilation if stale\n  - Cache-aware commands (inspect, symbol, graph-*, deps, impact, task)\n- **Git Snapshots:** Smart caching based on commit hash + dirty state\n- **Language Support:** Python, TypeScript default; configurable per repo\n- **Exclusion Patterns:** node_modules, __pycache__, .git, .venv, etc.\n\n#### **4. REST API** (`src/api/`)\n**Health & Info:**\n- `GET /` - Root info\n- `GET /health` - Service health\n- `GET /api/v1/info` - Features list\n\n**Search:** `POST /api/v1/search/`\n- Exact, fuzzy, or hybrid search\n- Returns scored symbol results\n\n**Ego Graph:** `POST /api/v1/ego/`\n- Symbol → connected nodes to depth N\n- Redis caching for performance\n\n**Impact Analysis:** `POST /api/v1/impact/`\n- Symbol → impacted downstream symbols\n- Depth-limited traversal\n\n**Scorecard:** `POST /api/v1/scorecard/scan`\n- AI-readiness scanning\n- Multiple detectors (docs, i18n, route coverage, etc.)\n- Background task support\n\n**Metrics:** `GET /metrics` - Prometheus endpoint\n\n#### **5. Rust Engine** (`rust/crates/aethyme-engine/`)\n**Core Modules:**\n- `graph.rs` - Graph representation & algorithms\n- `search.rs` - Symbol search with ranking\n- `navigation.rs` - Graph-mediated navigation\n- `task.rs` - Task planning & anchor detection\n- `context_pack.rs` - Context packing for AI\n- `anchors.rs` - Identifying high-priority entry points\n- `overview.rs` - Repo-level summaries\n- `signals.rs` - Navigability metrics (parser visibility, boundary clarity)\n- `indexer/` - Language-specific parsing (Python, TypeScript, Rust)\n- `passes/` - Multi-pass analysis (code, docs, configs, overlays)\n\n**CLI Binary:** `aethyme-engine-cli` - Direct invocation from Python layer\n\n#### **6. Scoring & Evaluation** (`src/scorecard/` & `src/eval/`)\n**Scorecard System:**\n- **Detectors:** ability_coverage, data_ui_coverage, i18n_gaps, route_coverage, generated_files, folder_docs, schema_drift, relative_links\n- **Engine:** Runs specified or all detectors, calculates aggregate score\n- **Output:** JSON & Markdown formatters\n\n**Evaluation Workflows:**\n- **explain-repo:** Baseline vs Aethyme comparison\n- **navigation-ctf:** Capture-the-flag navigation evaluation\n- **Control Prompts:** Baseline (raw inspect) vs Aethyme (graph-mediated navigation)\n- **Scoring Rubric:** Structured output validation\n\n#### **7. CLI** (`src/cli.py`)\n**Major Commands:**\n- `repo ingest` / `repo inspect` / `repo clear-cache`\n- `query symbol` / `query deps`\n- `graph node` / `graph children` / `graph callers` / `graph docs`\n- `task pack` / `task explain` / `task anchors` / `task scope` / `task next`\n- `eval explain-repo` / `eval navigation-ctf`\n\n**Output:** JSON or plain text, structured for programmatic use\n\n---\n\n### **Data Models**\n\n#### **Node** (src/models/graph.py)\n```python\n- symbol: str\n- file_path: str\n- line_number, column_number: int\n- kind: NodeKind (def, ref, file, class, function, method, variable, import)\n- language: str\n- signature, documentation, metadata: optional\n- id, display_id: computed\n```\n\n#### **Edge**\n```python\n- EdgeType: invoke, import, contain, inherit, implement, props_flow, return, parameter\n```\n\n#### **IndexingResult**\n```python\n- repository_id, name, path\n- org_id, tenant_id\n- total_nodes, total_edges, total_files\n- language_results[]\n```\n\n---\n\n### **Database Schema** (Inferred)\n- `aethyme.orgs` - Organizations\n- `aethyme.tenants` - Tenant isolation\n- `aethyme.repositories` - Indexed repositories\n- `aethyme.nodes` - Code symbols\n- `aethyme.edges` - Symbol relationships\n- Row-level security policies by `tenant_id`, `org_id`\n\n---\n\n### **Dependencies Summary**\n\n**Core Runtime:**\n- FastAPI (web framework), Uvicorn (ASGI server)\n- psycopg2 (PostgreSQL), redis (caching)\n- Pydantic (validation), Click (CLI)\n- structlog (structured logging), prometheus-client (metrics)\n- tree-sitter (parsing), python-jose (JWT)\n\n**Rust:**\n- rayon (parallelism)\n\n**Development:**\n- pytest, pytest-asyncio (testing)\n- ruff (linting), pyright (type checking)\n- black (formatting)\n\n---\n\n### **Key Features**\n\n1. **Multi-Tenant Isolation** - Strict tenant scoping with PostgreSQL RLS\n2. **Hybrid Search** - Full-text + fuzzy symbol search with ranking\n3. **Graph Traversal** - Ego graphs, impact analysis, dependency frontiers\n4. **Deterministic Navigation** - Rust-powered task-context packs for AI agents\n5. **AI-Readiness Scoring** - Automated code quality assessment\n6. **Local-First Workflow** - Works against single local repos without SaaS\n7. **Smart Caching** - Git-aware snapshot caching with fingerprinting\n8. **Production Ready** - Connection pooling, rate limiting, metrics, structured logging\n9. **Dual-Stack** - Rust for deterministic engines, Python for API/CLI orchestration\n\n---\n\n### **Test Files** (Comprehensive Coverage)\n\n- `tests/api/test_core_flow.py` - PostgreSQL-backed tests\n- `make lint`, `make type-check` - Code quality\n- `make migrate`, `make seed` - Database setup\n- `make rust-test`, `make rust-fmt` - Rust operations\n- `make openapi` - Generate OpenAPI spec\n\n**Entry Points:**\n1. **API:** `bash scripts/start-api.sh` → http://localhost:8001\n2. **CLI:** `python -m src.cli` or `aethyme` (after install)\n3. **Indexing:** Direct service calls or API endpoints\n\n---\n\nThis is a mature, production-grade code intelligence platform designed for AI-assisted repository navigation and analysis, with emphasis on deterministic behavior, multi-tenant security, and local-first capabilities."},{"type":"text","text":"agentId: ad518b12d7b066df4 (for resuming to continue this agent's work if needed)\n<usage>total_tokens: 89933\ntool_uses: 33\nduration_ms: 71054</usage>"}]}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"848984ce-8ac6-4110-815c-a094537eb36e","uuid":"eccdd2d1-cf74-470e-bd19-135b32eb5c74","tool_use_result":{"status":"completed","prompt":"Explore the repository at /Users/christophehenner/Downloads/Repositories/Aethyme/packages/aethyme thoroughly. ─────────────────────────────────────`\n**Dual-stack architecture pattern**: Aethyme uses Rust for the deterministic, CPU-intensive graph engine (invoked as a subprocess binary) and Python for the API/CLI orchestration layer. This is a common pattern for performance-critical backends — it lets each language do what it does best, while the Python layer handles I/O-bound work (HTTP, DB, Redis) and the Rust binary handles graph traversal and symbol parsing at native speed. The tradeoff is that the subprocess boundary means all data must be serialized (JSON) across the language boundary.\n\n**PostgreSQL RLS as a security primitive**: Rather than filtering queries in application code, Aethyme sets `app.current_tenant` and `app.current_org` as PostgreSQL session variables before each query, letting the DB enforce row-level security policies. This is a stronger isolation guarantee than application-layer filtering — even a buggy query can't leak cross-tenant data if the RLS policy is correct.\n\n**Git-aware caching for indexing**: The indexing layer fingerprints each repository snapshot by commit hash + dirty-state to invalidate caches. This is the right design for a code intelligence system — without it, stale graph data would cause incorrect navigation results for AI agents.\n`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`\n\nHere is the full structured explanation of the **Aethyme Core** package:\n\n---\n\n## What is it?\n\n**Aethyme Core** is a production-grade, **graph-based code intelligence platform** built to index, analyze, and navigate software repositories — primarily to give AI agents (and developers) deterministic, structured understanding of codebases. The canonical data hierarchy is:\n\n```\nPlatform → Org → Tenant → Repository → Graph\n```\n\n---\n\n## Architecture: Dual-Stack (Rust + Python)\n\n| Layer | Technology | Responsibility |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Engine** | Rust | Symbol parsing, graph traversal, context-pack generation, navigation signals |\n| **API / CLI** | Python (FastAPI + Click) | REST endpoints, CLI, auth, multi-tenancy, caching |\n| **Storage** | PostgreSQL | Graph nodes/edges with row-level security (RLS) per tenant |\n| **Cache** | Redis | Ego-graph query caching (300s TTL) |\n| **Frontend** | TypeScript + React 19 + Cytoscape | Graph visualization |\n\nThe Python layer shells out to a compiled Rust binary (`aethyme-engine-cli`) via subprocess for all compute-intensive work, passing data as JSON across the boundary.\n\n---\n\n## Core Capabilities\n\n- **Hybrid Symbol Search** — full-text + fuzzy, scored results\n- **Ego-Graph Traversal** — a symbol's connected neighborhood to depth N\n- **Impact Analysis** — downstream symbols affected by a change\n- **Context Packs** — structured AI task context from graph + anchors\n- **AI-Readiness Scorecard** — detectors for docs coverage, i18n gaps, route coverage, schema drift, etc.\n- **Automated Fixers** — patch generation + GitHub PR integration\n- **Eval Benchmarks** — baseline vs. Aethyme-augmented AI navigation comparison\n\n---\n\n## Key Entry Points\n\n| Purpose | Path |\n|---|---|\n| CLI | `src/cli.py` → registered as `aethyme` |\n| API server | `scripts/start-api.sh` → port 8001 |\n| Rust binary | `rust/crates/aethyme-engine/src/bin/aethyme-engine-cli.rs` |\n\n---\n\n## High-Risk Areas\n\nThe most security/correctness-sensitive code lives in:\n1. `src/auth/` — JWT/OIDC + tenant scoping (breaks multi-tenancy if wrong)\n2. `src/graph/store.py` — PostgreSQL RLS session variables (cross-tenant data leak risk)\n3. `src/indexing/engine.py` — Rust binary cache invalidation (silent stale-data bugs)\n4. `src/autofixers/safety.py` — Guards on automated repo mutation\n\n---\n\n## Recommended Reading Order\n\nStart with the data model (`src/models/graph.py`), then config, then the graph store, then the indexing service contract, then the Rust engine modules, then auth + API architecture pattern**: Aethyme uses Rust for the deterministic, CPU-intensive graph engine (invoked as a subprocess binary) and Python for the API/CLI orchestration layer. This is a common pattern for performance-critical backends \\u2014 it lets each language do what it does best, while the Python layer handles I/O-bound work (HTTP, DB, Redis) and the Rust binary handles graph traversal and symbol parsing at native speed. The tradeoff is that the subprocess boundary means all data must be serialized (JSON) across the language boundary.\\\\n\\\\n**PostgreSQL RLS as a security primitive**: Rather than filtering queries in application code, Aethyme sets `app.current_tenant` and `app.current_org` as PostgreSQL session variables before each query, letting the DB enforce row-level security policies. This is a stronger isolation guarantee than application-layer filtering \\u2014 even a buggy query can't leak cross-tenant data if the RLS policy is correct.\\\\n\\\\n**Git-aware caching for indexing**: The indexing layer fingerprints each repository snapshot by commit hash + dirty-state to invalidate caches. This is the right design for a code intelligence system \\u2014 without it, stale graph data would cause incorrect navigation results for AI agents.\\\\n`\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500\\u2500`\\\\n\\\\nHere is the full structured explanation of the **Aethyme Core** package:\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## What is it?\\\\n\\\\n**Aethyme Core** is a production-grade, **graph-based code intelligence platform** built to index, analyze, and navigate software repositories \\u2014 primarily to give AI agents (and developers) deterministic, structured understanding of codebases. The canonical data hierarchy is:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nPlatform \\u2192 Org \\u2192 Tenant \\u2192 Repository \\u2192 Graph\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Architecture: Dual-Stack (Rust +     1\u2192# Aethyme Core\\n     2\u2192\\n     3\u2192Last Updated: 2026-03-06\\n     4\u2192\\n     5\u2192Aethyme Core is the backend product in this repository.\\n     6\u2192\\n     7\u2192It owns:\\n     8\u2192\\n     9\u21921. repository indexing\\n    10\u21922. graph persistence and traversal\\n    11\u21923. search, ego graph, and impact analysis\\n    12\u21924. scorecard analysis\\n    13\u21925. controlled autofix tooling from the CLI\\n    14\u21926. deterministic navigation primitives for AI agents\\n    15\u2192\\n    16\u2192## Canonical Model\\n    17\u2192\\n    18\u2192`Platform > Org > Tenant > Repository > Graph`\\n    19\u2192\\n    20\u2192Runtime isolation is tenant-scoped.\\n    21\u2192\\n    22\u2192## Language Direction\\n    23\u2192\\n    24\u2192Aethyme is moving toward:\\n    25\u2192\\n    26\u2192- Rust for deterministic engine components\\n    27\u2192- Python for API, CLI, auth enforcement, scorecard orchestration, and SDKs\\n    28\u2192\\n    29\u2192See [`docs/architecture/rust-transition.md`](docs/architecture/rust-transition.md) and [`rust/README.md`](rust/README.md).\\n    30\u2192\\n    31\u2192## Auth Boundary\\n    32\u2192\\n    33\u2192- cloud owns login, registration, sessions, and user lifecycle\\n    34\u2192- core validates bearer credentials and API keys\\n    35\u2192- core enforces `org`, `tenant_id`, and `scopes`\\n    36\u2192- local development can mint a cloud-issued token for an existing user via `POST /api/auth/dev/token`\\n    37\u2192\\n    38\u2192## Active Surface\\n    39\u2192\\n    40\u2192### Core Logic\\n    41\u2192- `src/indexer`\\n    42\u2192- `src/indexing`\\n    43\u2192- `src/graph`\\n    44\u2192- `src/models`\\n    45\u2192- `src/scorecard`\\n    46\u2192- `src/autofixers`\\n    47\u2192- `rust`\\n    48\u2192\\n    49\u2192### Delivery\\n    50\u2192- `src/api`\\n    51\u2192- `src/cli.py`\\n    52\u2192- `sdk/python`\\n    53\u2192\\n    54\u2192### Verification\\n    55\u2192- `tests/api`\\n    56\u2192- `tests/queries`\\n    57\u2192- `tests/indexing`\\n    58\u2192- `tests/scorecard`\\n    59\u2192- `tests/autofixers`\\n    60\u2192\\n    61\u2192## Current Standard\\n    62\u2192\\n    63\u2192Only document and defend the verified path:\\n    64\u2192\\n    65\u2192- trusted bearer token or API key required\\n    66\u2192- `POST /api/v1/index/repositories`\\n    67\u2192- `POST /api/v1/search/`\\n    68\u2192- `POST /api/v1/ego/`\\n    69\u2192- `POST /api/v1/impact/`\\n    70\u2192- `POST /api/v1/scorecard/scan`\\n    71\u2192\\n    72\u2192API and CLI indexing both run through [`src/indexing/service.py`](src/indexing/service.py).\\n    73\u2192\\n    74\u2192## Local-First Workflow\\n    75\u2192\\n    76\u2192For the first product proof, Aethyme can run against one local repository without any SaaS layer.\\n    77\u2192\\n    78\u2192Core commands:\\n    79\u2192\\n    80\u2192- `aethyme repo ingest /path/to/repo`\\n    81\u2192- `aethyme repo inspect /path/to/repo --json-output`\\n    82\u2192- `aethyme repo clear-cache /path/to/repo`\\n    83\u2192- `aethyme query symbol /path/to/repo main`\\n    84\u2192- `aethyme query deps /path/to/repo src/main.py`\\n    85\u2192- `aethyme graph node /path/to/repo src/main.py --json-output`\\n    86\u2192- `aethyme graph children /path/to/repo GameEngine --json-output`\\n    87\u2192- `aethyme graph callers /path/to/repo fn:REPO:path:main --json-output`\\n    88\u2192- `aethyme graph docs /path/to/repo src/main.py --json-output`\\n    89\u2192- `aethyme task pack --repo /path/to/repo --task \\\"Explain this repo\\\" --json-output`\\n    90\u2192- `aethyme task explain --repo /path/to/repo`\\n    91\u2192- `aethyme task anchors --repo /path/to/repo --task \\\"Update validate_token flow\\\" --json-output`\\n    92\u2192- `aethyme task scope --repo /path/to/repo --task \\\"Update validate_token flow\\\" --json-output`\\n    93\u2192- `aethyme task next --repo /path/to/repo --task \\\"Update validate_token flow\\\" --json-output`\\n    94\u2192- `aethyme task expand --repo /path/to/repo --node src/auth.py --json-output`\\n    95\u2192- `aethyme eval explain-repo --repo /path/to/repo --json-output`\\n    96\u2192- `aethyme eval explain-repo --repo /path/to/repo --baseline-cmd \\\"<cmd>\\\" --aethyme-cmd \\\"<cmd>\\\"`\\n    97\u2192- `aethyme eval navigation-ctf --repo /path/to/repo --json-output`\\n    98\u2192\\n    99\u2192Codex runner example:\\n   100\u2192\\n   101\u2192- `aethyme eval explain-repo --repo /path/to/repo --baseline-cmd \\\"packages/aethyme/.venv/bin/python packages/aethyme/scripts/eval/run_codex_eval.py\\\" --aethyme-cmd \\\"packages/aethyme/.venv/bin/python packages/aethyme/scripts/eval/run_codex_eval.py\\\"`\\n   102\u2192\\n   103\u2192This local path is the shortest route to proving:\\n   104\u2192\\n   105\u21921. repository mapping\\n   106\u21922. architecture pattern**: Aethyme uses Rust for the deterministic, CPU-intensive graph engine (invoked as a subprocess binary) and Python for the API/CLI orchestration layer. This is a common pattern for performance-critical backends \u2014 it lets each language do what it does best, while the Python layer handles I/O-bound work (HTTP, DB, Redis) and the Rust binary handles graph traversal and symbol parsing at native speed. The tradeoff is that the subprocess boundary means all data must be serialized (JSON) across the language boundary.\\n\\n**PostgreSQL RLS as a security primitive**: Rather than filtering queries in application code, Aethyme sets `app.current_tenant` and `app.current_org` as PostgreSQL session variables before each query, letting the DB enforce row-level security policies. This is a stronger isolation guarantee than application-layer filtering \u2014 even a buggy query can't leak cross-tenant data if the RLS policy is correct.\\n\\n**Git-aware caching for indexing**: The indexing layer fingerprints each repository snapshot by commit hash + dirty-state to invalidate caches. navigation and code changes as\n deterministic and efficient as possible.\n\nThe engine layers that benefit most from Rust are:\n\n- fallback indexing and symbol extraction\n- graph expansion and traversal\n- deterministic context-pack assembly\n- scope and risk classification\n- later, advisory and enforceable policy evaluation\n\n## What Stays In Python\n\nFor now, Python remains responsible for:\n\n- API delivery\n- CLI delivery\n- auth and tenant enforcement\n- scorecard orchestration\n- SDKs\n- product experimentation around workflows\n\n## What Moves To Rust First\n\nPhase 1 Rust targets:\n\n1. context-pack data model\n2. deterministic pack-building pipeline\n3. risk and scope types\n4. repository mapping\n5. discoverability kernels\n\n## Current Local-First Surface\n\nThe Rust workspace now supports the first local-repo proof path behind the Python CLI:\n\n- repository inspection\n- symbol lookup\n- dependency frontier lookup\n- impact frontier lookup\n- deterministic task-context pack assembly\n- deterministic explain-repo output\n\nThe current entrypoint is the local engine binary invoked through Python adapters:\n\n- `cargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin aethyme-engine-cli -- inspect --repo /path/to/repo`\n- `cargo run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin aethyme-engine-cli -- pack --repo /path/to/repo --task \"Explain this repo\"`\n\nAt runtime, the Python layer now builds the binary once and executes the binary directly rather than shelling through `cargo run` on every request.\n\n## Rule\n\nDo not move customer-facing orchestration into Rust until the product semantics\nare stable.\n\nMove engine components Aethyme Core\n\nLast Updated: 2026-03-06\n\nAethyme Core is the backend product in this repository.\n\nIt owns:\n\n1. repository indexing\n2. graph persistence and traversal\n3. search, ego graph, and impact analysis\n4. scorecard analysis\n5. controlled autofix tooling from the CLI\n6. deterministic navigation primitives for AI agents\n\n## Canonical Model\n\n`Platform > Org > Tenant > Repository > Graph`\n\nRuntime isolation is tenant-scoped.\n\n## Language Direction\n\nAethyme is moving toward:\n\n- Rust for deterministic engine components\n- Python for API, CLI, auth enforcement, scorecard orchestration, and SDKs\n\nSee [`docs/architecture/rust-transition.md`](docs/architecture/rust-transition.md) and [`rust/README.md`](rust/README.md).\n\n## Auth Boundary\n\n- cloud owns login, registration, sessions, and user lifecycle\n- core validates bearer credentials and API keys\n- core enforces `org`, `tenant_id`, and `scopes`\n- local development can mint a cloud-issued token for an existing user via `POST /api/auth/dev/token`\n\n## Active Surface\n\n### Core Logic\n- `src/indexer`\n- `src/indexing`\n- `src/graph`\n- `src/models`\n- `src/scorecard`\n- `src/autofixers`\n- `rust`\n\n### Delivery\n- `src/api`\n- `src/cli.py`\n- `sdk/python`\n\n### Verification\n- `tests/api`\n- `tests/queries`\n- `tests/indexing`\n- `tests/scorecard`\n- `tests/autofixers`\n\n## Current Standard\n\nOnly document and defend the verified path:\n\n- trusted bearer token or API key required\n- `POST /api/v1/index/repositories`\n- `POST /api/v1/search/`\n- `POST /api/v1/ego/`\n- `POST /api/v1/impact/`\n- `POST /api/v1/scorecard/scan`\n\nAPI and CLI indexing both run through [`src/indexing/service.py`](src/indexing/service.py).\n\n## Local-First Workflow\n\nFor the first product proof, Aethyme can run against one local repository without any SaaS layer.\n\nCore commands:\n\n- `aethyme repo ingest /path/to/repo`\n- `aethyme repo inspect /path/to/repo --json-output`\n- `aethyme repo clear-cache /path/to/repo`\n- `aethyme query symbol /path/to/repo main`\n- `aethyme query deps /path/to/repo src/main.py`\n- `aethyme graph node /path/to/repo src/main.py --json-output`\n- `aethyme graph children /path/to/repo GameEngine --json-output`\n- `aethyme graph callers /path/to/repo fn:REPO:path:main --json-output`\n- `aethyme graph docs /path/to/repo src/main.py --json-output`\n- `aethyme task pack --repo /path/to/repo --task \"Explain this repo\" --json-output`\n- `aethyme task explain --repo /path/to/repo`\n- `aethyme task anchors --repo /path/to/repo --task \"Update validate_token flow\" --json-output`\n- `aethyme task scope --repo /path/to/repo --task \"Update validate_token flow\" --json-output`\n- `aethyme task next --repo /path/to/repo --task \"Update validate_token flow\" --json-output`\n- `aethyme task expand --repo /path/to/repo --node src/auth.py --json-output`\n- `aethyme eval explain-repo --repo /path/to/repo --json-output`\n- `aethyme eval explain-repo --repo /path/to/repo --baseline-cmd \"<cmd>\" --aethyme-cmd \"<cmd>\"`\n- `aethyme eval navigation-ctf --repo /path/to/repo --json-output`\n\nCodex runner example:\n\n- `aethyme eval explain-repo --repo /path/to/repo --baseline-cmd \"packages/aethyme/.venv/bin/python packages/aethyme/scripts/eval/run_codex_eval.py\" --aethyme-cmd \"packages/aethyme/.venv/bin/python packages/aethyme/scripts/eval/run_codex_eval.py\"`\n\nThis local path is the shortest route to proving:\n\n1. repository mapping\n2. discoverability\n3. graph-mediated navigation\n4. deterministic task-context packs\n5. explain-repo evaluation artifacts\n\nRuntime notes:\n\n- the Python layer now executes a built Rust binary rather than `cargo run` for every call\n- local repo artifacts are cached by snapshot key under `AETHYME_CACHE_DIR` or `/tmp/aethyme-cache`\n- Git repositories use commit plus dirty-state metadata for cache keys instead of a full recursive fingerprint on every call\n- `eval explain-repo` can execute real baseline and Aethyme runs when `--baseline-cmd` and `--aethyme-cmd` are provided\n- external runners receive `AETHYME_EVAL_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_FILE`, `AETHYME_EVAL_TOOL_REPO`, and `AETHYME_EVAL_TOOL_PYTHON` so Codex-style wrappers can enforce structured output and call back into Aethyme\n- the bundled Codex wrapper cleans its temporary prompt/event/schema files automatically; Chau7-driven runs should also close their MCP-controlled tab once the report artifact is captured and the tab is idle\n- without those commands, it still emits the comparison artifacts only\n- the Aethyme-assisted prompt now uses a compact rendered context-pack view instead of injecting the full raw pack\n- every `eval explain-repo` run writes a markdown report under `packages/aethyme/docs/reports/evals/`\n- the report includes the explanation, prompts, pack JSON, and verbose run results\n- eval outputs now include a structured output schema, scoring rubric, and reference answer\n\n## Start Here\n\n- [`../../docs/project-plan.md`](../../docs/project-plan.md)\n- [`docs/vision.md`](docs/vision.md)\n- `tests/scorecard`\\\\n- `tests/autofixers`\\\\n\\\\n## Current Standard\\\\n\\\\nOnly document and defend the verified path:\\\\n\\\\n- trusted bearer token or API key required\\\\n- `POST /api/v1/index/repositories`\\\\n- `POST /api/v1/search/`\\\\n- `POST /api/v1/ego/`\\\\n- `POST /api/v1/impact/`\\\\n- `POST /api/v1/scorecard/scan`\\\\n\\\\nAPI and CLI indexing both run through [`src/indexing/service.py`](src/indexing/service.py).\\\\n\\\\n## Local-First Workflow\\\\n\\\\nFor the first product proof, Aethyme can run against one local repository without any SaaS query symbol /path/to/repo main`\\\\n- `aethyme query deps /path/to/repo src/main.py`\\\\n- `aethyme graph node /path/to/repo src/main.py --json-output`\\\\n- `aethyme graph children /path/to/repo GameEngine --json-output`\\\\n- `aethyme graph callers /path/to/repo fn:REPO:path:main --json-output`\\\\n- `aethyme graph docs /path/to/repo src/main.py --json-output`\\\\n- `aethyme task pack --repo /path/to/repo --task \\\\\\\"Explain this repo\\\\\\\" --json-output`\\\\n- `aethyme task explain --repo /path/to/repo`\\\\n- `aethyme task anchors --repo /path/to/repo --task \\\\\\\"Update validate_token flow\\\\\\\" --json-output`\\\\n- `aethyme task scope --repo /path/to/repo --task \\\\\\\"Update validate_token flow\\\\\\\" --json-output`\\\\n- `aethyme task next --repo /path/to/repo --json-output`\\\\n- `aethyme eval explain-repo --repo /path/to/repo --baseline-cmd \\\\\\\"<cmd>\\\\\\\" --aethyme-cmd \\\\\\\"<cmd>\\\\\\\"`\\\\n- `aethyme eval navigation-ctf --repo /path/to/repo Aethyme Core\\n\\nLast Updated: 2026-03-06\\n\\nAethyme Core is the backend product in this repository.\\n\\nIt owns:\\n\\n1. repository indexing\\n2. graph persistence and traversal\\n3. search, ego graph, and impact analysis\\n4. scorecard analysis\\n5. controlled autofix tooling from the CLI\\n6. deterministic navigation primitives for AI agents\\n\\n## Canonical Model\\n\\n`Platform > Org > Tenant > Repository > Graph`\\n\\nRuntime isolation is tenant-scoped.\\n\\n## Language Direction\\n\\nAethyme is moving toward:\\n\\n- Rust for deterministic engine components\\n- Python for API, CLI, auth enforcement, scorecard orchestration, and SDKs\\n\\nSee [`docs/architecture/rust-transition.md`](docs/architecture/rust-transition.md) and [`rust/README.md`](rust/README.md).\\n\\n## Auth Boundary\\n\\n- cloud owns login, registration, sessions, and user lifecycle\\n- core validates bearer credentials and API keys\\n- core enforces `org`, `tenant_id`, and `scopes`\\n- local development can mint a cloud-issued token for an existing user via `POST /api/auth/dev/token`\\n\\n## Active Surface\\n\\n### Core Logic\\n- `src/indexer`\\n- `src/indexing`\\n- `src/graph`\\n- `src/models`\\n- `src/scorecard`\\n- `src/autofixers`\\n- `rust`\\n\\n### Delivery\\n- `src/api`\\n- `src/cli.py`\\n- `sdk/python`\\n\\n### Verification\\n- `tests/api`\\n- `tests/queries`\\n- `tests/indexing`\\n- `tests/scorecard`\\n- `tests/autofixers`\\n\\n## Current Standard\\n\\nOnly document and defend the verified path:\\n\\n- trusted bearer token or API key required\\n- `POST /api/v1/index/repositories`\\n- `POST /api/v1/search/`\\n- `POST /api/v1/ego/`\\n- `POST /api/v1/impact/`\\n- `POST /api/v1/scorecard/scan`\\n\\nAPI and CLI indexing both run through [`src/indexing/service.py`](src/indexing/service.py).\\n\\n## Local-First Workflow\\n\\nFor the first product proof, Aethyme can run against one local repository without any SaaS layer.\\n\\nCore commands:\\n\\n- `aethyme repo ingest /path/to/repo`\\n- `aethyme repo inspect /path/to/repo --json-output`\\n- `aethyme repo clear-cache /path/to/repo`\\n- `aethyme query symbol /path/to/repo main`\\n- `aethyme query deps /path/to/repo src/main.py`\\n- `aethyme graph node /path/to/repo src/main.py --json-output`\\n- `aethyme graph children /path/to/repo GameEngine --json-output`\\n- `aethyme graph callers /path/to/repo fn:REPO:path:main --json-output`\\n- `aethyme graph docs /path/to/repo src/main.py --json-output`\\n- `aethyme task pack --repo /path/to/repo --task \\\"Explain this repo\\\" --json-output`\\n- `aethyme task explain --repo /path/to/repo`\\n- `aethyme task anchors --repo /path/to/repo --task \\\"Update validate_token flow\\\" --json-output`\\n- `aethyme task scope --repo /path/to/repo --task \\\"Update validate_token flow\\\" --json-output`\\n- `aethyme task next --repo /path/to/repo --task \\\"Update validate_token flow\\\" --json-output`\\n- `aethyme task expand --repo /path/to/repo --node src/auth.py --json-output`\\n- `aethyme eval explain-repo --repo /path/to/repo --json-output`\\n- `aethyme eval explain-repo --repo /path/to/repo --baseline-cmd \\\"<cmd>\\\" --aethyme-cmd \\\"<cmd>\\\"`\\n- `aethyme eval navigation-ctf --repo /path/to/repo --json-output`\\n\\nCodex runner example:\\n\\n- `aethyme eval explain-repo --repo /path/to/repo --baseline-cmd \\\"packages/aethyme/.venv/bin/python packages/aethyme/scripts/eval/run_codex_eval.py\\\" --aethyme-cmd \\\"packages/aethyme/.venv/bin/python packages/aethyme/scripts/eval/run_codex_eval.py\\\"`\\n\\nThis local path is the shortest route to proving:\\n\\n1. repository mapping\\n2. discoverability\\n3. graph-mediated navigation\\n4. deterministic task-context packs\\n5. explain-repo evaluation artifacts\\n\\nRuntime notes:\\n\\n- the Python layer now executes a built Rust binary rather than `cargo run` for every call\\n- local repo artifacts are cached by snapshot key under `AETHYME_CACHE_DIR` or `/tmp/aethyme-cache`\\n- Git repositories use commit plus dirty-state metadata for cache keys instead of a full recursive fingerprint on every call\\n- `eval explain-repo` can execute real baseline and Aethyme runs when `--baseline-cmd` and `--aethyme-cmd` are provided\\n- external runners receive `AETHYME_EVAL_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_FILE`, `AETHYME_EVAL_TOOL_REPO`, and `AETHYME_EVAL_TOOL_PYTHON` so Codex-style wrappers can enforce structured output and call back into Aethyme\\n- the bundled Codex wrapper cleans its temporary prompt/event/schema files automatically; Chau7-driven runs should also close their MCP-controlled tab once the report artifact is captured and the tab is idle\\n- without those commands, it still emits the comparison artifacts only\\n- the Aethyme-assisted prompt now uses a compact rendered context-pack view instead of injecting the full raw pack\\n- every `eval explain-repo` run writes a markdown report under `packages/aethyme/docs/reports/evals/`\\n- the report includes the explanation, prompts, pack JSON, and verbose run results\\n- eval outputs now include a structured output schema, scoring rubric, and reference answer\\n\\n## Start Here\\n\\n- [`../../docs/project-plan.md`](../../docs/project-plan.md)\\n- [`docs/vision.md`](docs/vision.md)\\n-
